title: What if the hundredth year gets no leap day?
description: With no leap day in the hundredth year, the video counts the days in a hundred and in a thousand calendar years and compares them with the Earth.
teaching_notes: One idea: leaving out the leap day in the hundredth year brings the calendar back close to the Earth, but in a thousand years it falls a little behind. Watch for children who still count twenty five leap years in a hundred years.

source: With no leap day in the 100th year, how many days are in 100 calendar years and in 1000 calendar years? Compare with the Earth.
video_script.why: The child has seen the calendar run ahead of the Earth with a leap day in every fourth year, and now removes the leap day from the hundredth year to see what changes.
video_script.substitution: the book's own hundred and thousand calendar years with no leap day in the hundredth year, against the Earth's three hundred and sixty five point two four two two days a trip
video_script.anchor: A hundred calendar years with no leap day in the hundredth year, and a thousand years made of ten such blocks
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip still counts twenty five leap years in a hundred years. But the hundredth year gets no leap day, so only twenty four leap years remain.
video_script.payoff_line: The gap in a thousand years is now known.

final_answer.value: 36524 days in 100 years; 365240 against 365242.2 in 1000 years, a gap of 2.2 days
final_answer.spoken: thirty six thousand five hundred and twenty four days in a hundred years, and three hundred and sixty five thousand two hundred and forty days against three hundred and sixty five thousand two hundred and forty two point two days in a thousand years, a gap of two point two days

maths_rules: years divisible by 4 in 100 years: 100 ÷ 4 = 25, but the 100th year gets no leap day, so 24 leap years; plain years = 100 − 24 = 76
1000 years are ten blocks of 100 years: 36524 × 10 = 365240 days
365242.2 − 365240 = 2.2, so the calendar is behind the Earth by 2.2 days
the slip: 25 leap years in 100 years
video_script.design: One idea: with the hundredth year leaving out its leap day, a hundred years come very close to the Earth, but a thousand years leave a small gap the other way. Assumes the videos on four and a hundred years. Wrong idea: the hundredth year still gets its leap day. The gap of two point two stays hidden until the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, count the days in a hundred calendar years.

<bookmark mark='m4'/>Adding the two gives thirty six thousand five hundred and twenty four days.
